title: ORBIT: Oak Ridge Base Foundation Model for Earth System Predictability
problem: Earth system predictability is challenged by the complexity of environmental dynamics and multitude of variables. Current AI foundation models are constrained by their size and data integration, limiting their effectiveness in addressing Earth system prediction challenges.
motivation: Improving Earth system predictability through scaling foundation models is critical for addressing complex environmental dynamics that current AI systems cannot adequately handle.
method: ORBIT is a vision transformer—an AI model trained on satellite imagery that learns patterns by analyzing images in small sections—scaled to 113 billion parameters, the individual numerical settings the model learns. To train this enormous model, the team distributed it across 49,152 AMD GPUs using a hybrid parallelism technique that divides both the model and the data simultaneously in orthogonal ways, keeping the computational work balanced across all hardware. Running on Oak Ridge's Frontier supercomputer, ORBIT sustained 684 petaFLOPS to 1.6 exaFLOPS with 41–85% scaling efficiency, achieving 41–85% of theoretical peak performance as tens of thousands of GPUs work together.
key_novelty: A parallelism technique called tensor-data orthogonal parallelism that splits both an AI model and its training data simultaneously across GPUs, enabling Earth system vision transformers to scale 1000 times larger than existing models.
contributions: Scaled vision transformer to 113 billion parameters, 1000x larger than existing climate AI foundation models
Novel hybrid tensor-data orthogonal parallelism technique for efficient distributed training
Achieved 684 petaFLOPS to 1.6 exaFLOPS sustained throughput on Frontier supercomputer
Demonstrated 41-85% scaling efficiency across 49,152 AMD GPUs
